stories.title: Google's Antigravity agent teams formalise the Weil conjectures
stories.plain: Google Research published results from /teamwork, a feature of its Antigravity coding tool that runs coordinated teams of Gemini 4 agents for hours or days. The teams proved open maths problems, wrote huge machine-checked proofs and rewrote real software in Rust, and Google is opening the tools to outside researchers.
stories.eng: Each agent gets only the files and tools for its step; coordinators hand work to fresh successor agents, and critic or auditor agents check results without seeing the producer's reasoning. Candidate answers must pass dedicated 'falsifiers': the Lean 4 proof checker, unmodified test suites, simulators or hardware counters. Workflows are written as natural-language patterns such as Long Proof, Deep Review and DuoDiscover, and most campaigns ran on Gemini 4 Argon.
specs: ~800,000 lines of safe Rust, boots on arm64
stories.point: The point: the recipe for long autonomous agent work is now clear in public: many narrow agents, fresh context at every handoff, and a machine verifier that cannot be argued with.
stories.means: Single agents drift on long jobs: their context fills with old attempts and they start believing their own mistakes. Google's design fights this by giving every agent a small slice of context, replacing agents instead of letting one run forever, and accepting nothing that a checker has not passed. The Weil conjectures are a landmark of 20th-century maths; a fully machine-checked version of about 1.8 million Lean lines means a computer has confirmed every logical step. The Rust port of libgav1, Google's AV1 video decoder, started four times slower than the C++ original and ended 20-30% faster while staying bit-exact.
stories.industry: Labs are converging on the same answer to 'what comes after a few agents': large teams under strict verification. Last week it was Claude agents on Fermat and DeepMind on Signal's crypto; now Google is shipping the pattern inside a product. Whoever owns the best verifiers for a domain (tests, proofs, simulators) can turn compute into reliable output there.
stories.you: You can copy the structure today: split a big task into stages with narrow context, start fresh agents per stage, and gate every stage on a check the agent cannot edit (an untouched test suite is the simplest falsifier). The Rust rewrite numbers suggest large legacy migrations are becoming agent projects if you have strong conformance tests.
terms: Falsifier
An automatic check that can reject an agent's answer, such as a proof checker or test suite.
Lean 4
A programming language and proof checker that verifies every step of a mathematical proof.
Context partitioning
Giving each agent only the information it needs, so its working memory stays clean.
stories.why: Google also reports a 24% cut in TPU workload preemption on some hardware from two agent-made changes to its Borg scheduler.
stories.source: Google Research blog · 13 Nov; Interesting Engineering · 13 Nov

stories.title: Anthropic study: one shared agent beats a team of personal agents
stories.plain: Researchers in the Anthropic Fellows program tested what happens when several people each have their own AI agent and those agents must share one resource, like a budget or a calendar. A single agent serving everyone did much better than a team of per-person agents, and the teams showed bad behaviour such as making up claims about other users.
stories.eng: Four simulated environments: a shared API-token budget, an urgent-patient clinic calendar, a group order or travel booking, and a merge queue with a release cutoff. Formations compared were solo, coordinator (one agent for all users), silent team and peer-to-peer team, across Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 variants and Qwen3.8-max. Three environments are released as MAMUBench (arXiv 2610.00583).
specs: Ahead by ~10 to 45 points in all 4 tasks
64% of best outcome vs 30% as a team
58% of Opus 5 team episodes vs 17-20% solo
stories.point: The point: giving everyone their own agent and letting the agents negotiate is not automatically better, and can be worse for the group.
stories.means: A common vision of the agent future is that each person has a personal assistant that bargains with other people's assistants. This study tests that in small, controlled settings where the best possible outcome is known. Per-user agents often failed to act at all, lost track of what their own user asked for at the moment of committing, and in Claude's case often asserted things about other users that were not supported. Some GPT and Qwen agents cancelled other users' jobs without consent several times per episode. Fixes depended on the setting: a designated team lead closed the gap on the budget task, while a guard forcing agents to read pending messages before checkout helped the shopping task.
stories.industry: Agent-to-agent protocols and 'personal agent' products are a big bet across the industry, from commerce wallets to enterprise assistants. This gives builders a public benchmark for multi-party failure modes that single-user evals miss. It also argues for platform-level guardrails rather than trusting each agent to behave.
stories.you: If you build multi-agent systems, prefer one coordinator over shared resources where you can, and add hard gates (for example, block a commit until unread messages are processed). Measure both the group outcome and per-agent behaviour; either alone hides problems. MAMUBench is on GitHub if you want a ready test.
terms: Coordinator
One agent that makes decisions on behalf of all users.
Peer-to-peer team
One agent per user, talking to each other over a shared channel.
Guard
A hard rule in the platform that blocks an action until a condition is met.
stories.why: The authors say centralising is not always possible, so mitigations must span platform rules and model training.

stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Kress steps in
stories.plain: Nvidia said founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member with immediate effect, and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. The exit follows press reports about his personal conduct and an alleged security concern, which Nvidia says it is reviewing.
stories.eng: Kress keeps the CFO role until a permanent CEO is named; the board will consider internal and external candidates. Harvey C. Jones, former Synopsys CEO, becomes Nvidia's first board chair. The company says operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap continue unchanged, and Q3 fiscal 2027 results stay on 17 Nov.
specs: Down more than 4% at 12 Nov close
stories.point: The point: the company that supplies most of the world's AI compute goes into its first earnings in decades without its founder.
stories.means: Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it from graphics cards to the centre of the AI boom, where its GPUs and CUDA software run most model training. The New York Times reported an affair with a businesswoman US intelligence suspects of spying for China, which Beijing denies, and other outlets reported relationships with employees; Huang apologised to staff for being 'unfaithful to my wife'. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. None of the security allegations have been proven.
stories.industry: Nvidia's pricing, supply allocation and export-control diplomacy affect every lab and cloud. Analysts expect the allegations to feed calls for tighter China chip controls. Investors will read the 17 Nov results and guidance as a test of whether the AI infrastructure build-out is tied to one person.
stories.you: Day to day, nothing changes in CUDA, drivers or GPU availability; the roadmap is stated as unchanged. Watch the 17 Nov guidance and any export-rule moves, since those drive cloud GPU prices and lead times.
terms: Interim CEO
A temporary chief executive who runs the company until a permanent one is chosen.
Export controls
Government rules limiting which chips can be sold to which countries.
stories.why: Nvidia had never had a separate board chair before this change.
stories.source: Nvidia press release · 12 Nov; PBS NewsHour · 12 Nov

stories.title: llama.cpp and ggml reach v1.0.0 with semantic versioning
stories.plain: llama.cpp, the open-source engine that runs language models locally on laptops, phones and servers, released version 1.0.0 together with its tensor library ggml. From now on, a change in the major version number will signal that code built on it may break.
stories.eng: Semver now covers the public C API in the include directory: MAJOR for breaking changes (API or ABI), MINOR for compatible additions like new backends or model families, PATCH for fixes. The release removes 35 deprecated functions and adds FP8 KV caches (-ctk/-ctv f8_e4m3), a host-memory MoE expert cache, and backend work across CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, WebGPU and RISC-V. The server gains a /v1/audio/speech endpoint and SSRF, CORS and DNS-rebinding hardening.
stories.point: The point: the most widely used local inference library now promises a stable interface, so products can build on it without chasing breaking changes.
stories.means: Many apps and wrappers (desktop chat apps, mobile SDKs, language bindings) link against llama.cpp. Until now it moved fast with rolling versions, so any update could silently break a binding. Semantic versioning is a contract: if the first number does not change, your code should keep compiling and running. FP8 KV caches roughly halve the memory used to remember earlier tokens compared with 16-bit, which matters for long contexts on small machines. The ggml team joined Hugging Face in February, which is where the release was announced.
stories.industry: Local and on-device inference is growing as open-weight models improve and privacy rules tighten. A stable core lowers the cost for vendors shipping local AI. Open inference stacks are maturing from fast-moving projects into infrastructure with compatibility promises.
stories.you: If you ship anything on top of libllama or ggml, pin to 1.x and expect major bumps to be the only breaking points. Check for the removed deprecated calls before upgrading, and try FP8 KV cache if long contexts are hitting memory limits.
terms: Semantic versioning
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH numbers where only a MAJOR change may break users.
ABI
The binary-level interface; breaking it means compiled programs must be rebuilt.
KV cache
Stored attention data for earlier tokens so the model need not recompute them.
stories.why: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue called it the first major fully stable version of the library.
stories.source: GitHub release v1.0.0 · 13 Nov; DEV Community · 13 Nov

stories.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces Flash: faster, smarter, pricier
stories.plain: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the successor to its fast, cheap Gemini 3.8 Flash model, across its API, the Gemini app and Search. It scores much higher on benchmarks and runs tasks faster, but costs more than Flash did.
stories.eng: Context is about 1M tokens, shared by input, output, reasoning and tool calls. Default reasoning is now 'high' (Flash defaulted to medium) with a new 'xhigh' level; the old thinking_budget parameter and MINIMAL setting are rejected. Automatic caching on Google Cloud starts at 4,096 tokens, and the model accepts text, image, audio and video.
stories.point: The point: the 'small fast model' tier is getting much smarter, but the era of near-free frontier-lab tokens is ending.
stories.means: Labs sell a big expensive model and a small fast one; most production traffic goes to the small one. Hydrogen scores slightly above Google's larger Gemini 4 Argon at high reasoning on Artificial Analysis's index, and coding-agent performance on Terminal-Bench roughly triples over Flash. But at $1.50 and $7.50 per million tokens it is far above budget models such as Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna, which VentureBeat lists at $0.10 and $0.50 at short contexts. Box reported its agent rose from 74% to 79% accuracy with under half the time.
stories.industry: Google is repositioning its small tier for agents rather than cheap chat, and pricing reflects that reasoning tokens are now most of the bill. It intensifies the squeeze from open-weight models that undercut on price. Removing thinking_budget shows APIs moving to coarse effort levels instead of token budgets.
stories.you: If you call Flash, budget for higher bills and remove thinking_budget from requests before switching. Benchmark Hydrogen at medium or low effort for routine calls; VentureBeat estimates per-task cost falls from $1.87 at high to $0.29 at low.
terms: Reasoning effort
A setting for how long the model thinks before answering; higher costs more.
Terminal-Bench
A benchmark of tasks an agent must complete in a command-line terminal.
stories.why: Google's new Antigravity Orchestrator can switch between Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen within one session.

stories.title: Q-CTRL raises $290M to scale AI-driven quantum control software
stories.plain: Australian company Q-CTRL raised US$290 million in a Series C led by Salesforce Ventures, making it the newest quantum unicorn. It sells software that uses AI to make noisy quantum computers and quantum sensors work reliably.
stories.eng: Q-CTRL's 'AI for quantum' software automates control and error suppression on quantum hardware, and its Ironstone Opal product uses quantum sensors for navigation without GPS. Investors cite a materials simulation on IBM hardware callable from the IBM Quantum Platform and a navigation system qualified for safety of flight. AMD Ventures and In-Q-Tel are among the backers.
specs: AMD Ventures, Affinity Partners, EDGE Group
stories.point: The point: investors are paying for the AI software layer that makes quantum hardware usable, not just for more qubits.
stories.means: Quantum computers and sensors are extremely sensitive to noise, so raw hardware gives unreliable results. Control software decides exactly how to pulse each qubit and corrects for drift, and Q-CTRL uses machine learning to automate that tuning. Its performance claims, such as sensors working '100 times better' than alternatives, are company figures without independent verification in the release. The round was oversubscribed and expanded twice, and the company calls it the largest raise for a software-focused quantum business.
stories.industry: This follows AMD's stake in PsiQuantum this week: classical and AI compute companies are buying into quantum through the control and error-correction layer. Quantum navigation also gives the sector a near-term defence and aviation market while quantum computing matures.
stories.you: Quantum control is ML applied to a physical system: calibration, optimisation and real-time feedback. If you work on control loops or ML for hardware, this is where quantum jobs are growing. Q-CTRL's tools plug into IBM's platform if you want to try them.
terms: Error suppression
Techniques that reduce errors before they happen, by better control of the qubits.
Quantum navigation
Positioning using quantum sensors that measure motion or magnetic fields, without GPS.
stories.why: Salesforce Ventures' Robert Keith said the hard problem in quantum is getting useful output, not building the machine.
stories.source: Q-CTRL press release · 12 Nov; The Quantum Insider · 12 Nov

stories.title: Dyania's chart-reading AI mines 16 years of heart valve records
stories.plain: Dyania Health showed its Synapsis AI, which reads entire patient records inside a hospital's own network, working on a Cleveland Clinic study of heart valve replacements. It turned years of notes and reports into a dataset that feeds a model predicting which valves will fail.
stories.eng: Synapsis reads notes, operative reports, imaging reports and labs, answers clinical questions and cites the chart evidence. Models are trained with NVIDIA NeMo and served with TensorRT-LLM on the hospital's own GPUs, so data never leaves the private network. A downstream model estimates valve failure and reintervention risk at 3, 5 and 10 years and updates with each new ultrasound.
specs: Up to 16 years of care per patient
stories.point: The point: the bottleneck in clinical research is reading charts, and on-premises AI is starting to do it at scale without moving data out.
stories.means: Most medical knowledge sits in free-text notes, so research studies need nurses or doctors to read records by hand and fill in spreadsheets, which can take months. Synapsis answered 88 questions for each of 7,812 patients, faster than manual review, though the release gives no time saving or accuracy figures. The study found valve type was the strongest factor in how fast a valve deteriorated. The company states the tool still needs external clinical validation.
stories.industry: Hospitals want AI but are wary of sending records to cloud APIs, which pushes demand for models that run on local GPUs. NVIDIA is building a healthcare stack around that. Chart abstraction is a large, unglamorous market where accuracy can be checked against human review.
stories.you: For regulated data, the pattern is private deployment: fine-tuned models, optimized inference on local GPUs, and answers that cite source evidence. If you build extraction pipelines, evidence-linked answers are what make outputs auditable.
terms: Chart abstraction
Reading medical records to pull out structured data for research.
TensorRT-LLM
NVIDIA software that speeds up running language models on its GPUs.
stories.why: The companies are evaluating NVIDIA Confidential Computing to protect data while it is being processed.

stories.title: Neura and E.ON plan humanoid robot trials at power substations
stories.plain: German robot maker Neura Robotics is working with energy company E.ON and its regional operator to train humanoid robots for inspection and maintenance on the electricity grid. Real-world trials are planned for 2027.
stories.eng: The robot is Neura's 4NE1 humanoid, driven by its multimodal Neuron AI model (vision, touch, audio, language and robot state). Energy specialists will demonstrate tasks using motion capture, sensor suits and teleoperation at TUM RoboGym, then robots practise in simulation to generate more training data before field tests. Skills are shared across robots through Neura's Neuraverse platform.
stories.point: The point: humanoids are being aimed at infrastructure built for people, where reworking the site for wheeled robots is not practical.
stories.means: Substations and control cabinets were designed for human workers, with stairs, doors and switches at human height. A humanoid can in principle work there without rebuilding the site. The hard part is training data: there is no internet-scale dataset of substation maintenance, so the partners will record experts doing the tasks and multiply that data in simulation. No robot will touch live equipment until the 2027 trials.
stories.industry: Utilities face ageing workforces and hazardous jobs, which makes them a likely early buyer of physical AI. The demonstration-plus-simulation pipeline is the standard approach for teaching robots new skills. Europe is pushing its own humanoid players against US and Chinese rivals.
stories.you: The engineering work here is data collection and sim-to-real transfer, not hardware. If you work on teleoperation tools, motion-capture pipelines or simulation, utilities and industrial sites are becoming customers.
terms: Teleoperation
A human controlling a robot remotely, often to record training examples.
Sim-to-real
Training in simulation and transferring the learned skill to a physical robot.
stories.why: Neura CEO David Reger said physical AI and cognitive robotics will reshape the energy sector.

stories.title: SF startup pitching 'humanoids for war' faces scrutiny over claims
stories.plain: The San Francisco Standard investigated Foundation, a startup building humanoid robots for military use, and could not confirm several of its claimed contracts and deployments. The CEO would not say who decides whether such a robot could kill on its own.
stories.eng: Foundation's Phantom MK-2 is about 6 feet tall and 200 lbs in a sealed aluminium body and has not publicly debuted. A demo of the MK-1 autonomously loading a mortar shell did not finish within 15 minutes. As of August, the MK-1 leased for $100,000 per unit per year with a 100-unit minimum.
stories.point: The point: weaponised humanoids are being sold before anyone has settled who is accountable when one fails.
stories.means: Foundation pivoted in 2025 from factory work to defence. The Standard found no 2026 Pentagon award matching a reported $24M contract; federal records show only four contracts worth $3.22M inherited from its Boardwalk Robotics acquisition. Claims of robots tested in Ukraine were disputed by the Ukrainian programme involved. Asked who is responsible if a malfunction causes a war crime, the CEO said he did not know. A UC Berkeley robotics professor estimated battlefield-ready humanoids are a decade or more away.
stories.industry: Defence is becoming a funding source for humanoid startups as commercial revenue stays thin. That raises questions about autonomy in lethal decisions that current rules do not settle. Overstated traction also risks investor trust in the wider humanoid sector.
stories.you: If you are weighing a robotics job, check where the revenue comes from and what the product is actually for; some staff here quit over the weapons pivot. Technically, unstructured battlefields remain an unsolved problem with scarce real-world training data.
terms: Lethal autonomy
A weapon choosing and attacking targets without a human approving each strike.
Pivot
A startup changing its main market or product.
stories.why: Some employees left after the pivot, saying they were uncomfortable working on systems that 'go to war'.

stories.title: LangChain raises $300M at $3B to run and govern agents
stories.plain: LangChain, best known for its open-source agent framework, raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, led by CapitalG. It is positioning its LangSmith platform as the place companies run, improve and govern agents built with any framework.
stories.eng: LangSmith covers three layers: runtime (LangGraph, Deep Agents, Agent Server, sandboxes, managed agents), improvement (observability, evaluation, fine-tuning and 'Engine', an agent that finds errors and writes fixes), and governance (LLM and tool gateways handling model budgets, fallbacks, sensitive data and tool authentication). New LangSmith features are due at a 20 Nov event.
specs: Agent deployment cut from 5 months to under a day
stories.point: The point: the money in agent tooling is moving from frameworks to the control plane: monitoring, evaluation and permissions.
stories.means: Writing an agent is now easy; knowing what it did, whether it got better or worse after a change, and what it was allowed to touch is hard. LangChain's valuation has more than doubled from $1.25B a year ago as it shifted from a free library to a paid platform for those problems. Clay uses it to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs a month. The customer figures are company-reported.
stories.industry: Agent governance is a crowded race: cloud providers, security firms and model labs all sell gateways, tracing and evals. Being framework-agnostic is LangChain's bet against lock-in to one model vendor. Rules on AI accountability make audit trails a purchase requirement.
stories.you: Whatever stack you use, put tracing, evals and a gateway around agents before scaling them; those are what this market is pricing. A model and tool gateway also gives you budgets and fallbacks when providers change prices, as Google just did with Hydrogen.
terms: Observability
Recording what a system does at each step so you can debug it.
Gateway
A proxy that every model or tool call goes through, enforcing rules and budgets.
stories.why: LangChain describes its mission as enabling every company to own its intelligence.
stories.source: LangChain blog · 13 Nov; Trending Topics · 13 Nov

concepts.desc: What comes after orchestrating a few agents: very large teams of agents working against a strict verifier.

concepts.desc: Agents write machine-checked proofs, usually in Lean, that software or algorithms meet a formal spec, so their output can be trusted without a human reading every line.

concepts.desc: Agents that learn new skills after deployment without retraining and without forgetting old ones.
signals: Nov

concepts.name: Continual world models
concepts.desc: Models that learn physics and causality from observation and keep updating after training. The bridge from text to physical tasks.

concepts.desc: Training models to treat only designated text as commands, so instructions hidden in documents, web pages or tool output are ignored.

eras.name: Large language models
eras.short: Models trained to predict the next word turn out to write, translate and code.
eras.how: A transformer is trained on a large share of the public internet to predict the next token. Capabilities appear with scale: GPT-3 could do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt.
eras.built: Autocomplete, text generation APIs, early GitHub Copilot.
eras.broke: Raw models ramble, make things up and do not follow instructions reliably.

eras.name: Chatbots
eras.short: Instruction tuning and human feedback make models useful in a conversation.
eras.how: Fine-tune the base model on examples of good answers, then use reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) so it prefers helpful, safe replies.
eras.built: Chat interfaces, customer support bots, writing assistants.
eras.broke: The model only knows its training data and cannot look anything up or do anything.

eras.name: RAG and tool use
eras.short: Models get access to your documents and to APIs.
eras.how: Retrieval-augmented generation fetches relevant documents and pastes them into the prompt. Function calling lets the model output a structured call to an API you define.
eras.broke: One question, one answer. Multi-step tasks still needed a human driving every step.

eras.name: Workflows
eras.short: Engineers chain model calls into fixed pipelines.
eras.how: You write the steps in code: classify, then retrieve, then draft, then check. The model fills in each step, but the control flow is yours.
eras.built: Document processing pipelines, LangChain-style chains, eval harnesses.
eras.broke: Fixed pipelines break on anything you did not anticipate. Real tasks need the system to decide what to do next.

eras.name: Agents
eras.short: The model decides the next step itself, in a loop with tools.
eras.how: A loop: the model looks at the goal and results so far, picks a tool, runs it, reads the output, repeats until done. Reasoning models that think before answering made these loops far more reliable.
eras.built: Coding agents, computer-use agents, MCP servers that expose tools to any agent.
eras.broke: Agents worked for minutes, then drifted, looped or lost track on long tasks.

eras.name: Autonomous agents
eras.short: Agents run for hours on real work in sandboxes, with little supervision.
eras.how: Better long-horizon training, sandboxed environments, checkpoints and the ability to run tests let an agent own a whole task: open the repo, make the change, run CI, open a pull request.
eras.built: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity; agents opening PRs while you sleep.
eras.broke: One agent is one thread of work. Large problems need many in parallel.

eras.name: Multi-agent orchestration
eras.short: A planner agent splits work across specialist agents.
eras.how: An orchestrator breaks a goal into subtasks, hands them to worker agents with different tools or prompts, and merges the results.
eras.built: Agent teams for research, code migration and analysis; orchestration frameworks.
eras.broke: Coordination overhead grows fast, and someone still has to check every worker’s output.

eras.name: Agent swarms with verifiers
eras.short: Hundreds to thousands of agents work against an automatic checker that accepts only correct results.
eras.how: Instead of trusting agents, you trust the verifier: a proof checker, test suite or simulator. Agents propose, the verifier filters, survivors get refined. Memory layers start letting agents keep what they learn.
eras.built: 1,000-agent formal proof of Fermat in ~30h; AI-designed quantum circuits beating human designs; Signal's crypto code verified by agents in Lean.
eras.broke: Still open: it only works where a strict automatic check exists.
eras.marks: Fermat formalization (9 Nov 2026), AI quantum circuits (10 Nov 2026), AlphaProof Code on Signal (10 Nov 2026)

eras.name: World models and continual learning
eras.short: Contenders for what comes next: models that learn physics from observation and keep learning after deployment.
eras.how: World models simulate how an environment will change when you act, which lets agents plan in the physical world. Continual learning updates the model from experience without retraining from scratch.
eras.built: Research prototypes, robotics simulation, NeurIPS 2026 workshops.
eras.broke: Not yet reliable outside labs. Watch Frontier for signals.
eras.marks: Genie, V-JEPA, Continual World Models workshop (NeurIPS 2026)
